title: General Science Test 1 (Physics & Chemistry — most probable)

questions.q: The unit of force in the International System of Units (SI) is:
questions.explain: Force is measured in newtons (N); Joule = energy, Watt = power, Pascal = pressure.

questions.q: The unit of energy and work in the International System of Units (SI) is:
questions.explain: Work and energy share the unit Joule; power (rate of doing work) is the Watt.

questions.q: The unit of power in the International System of Units (SI) is:
questions.explain: One watt = one joule per second; the kilowatt-hour (unit of electricity bill) is a unit of energy, not power.

questions.q: The unit of pressure in the International System of Units (SI) is:
questions.explain: Pressure is measured in pascals (N/m²); atmospheric pressure is about 101,325 Pa.

questions.q: The unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI) is:
questions.explain: Frequency (cycles per second) is Hertz; decibel measures sound intensity level.

questions.q: The unit of electric resistance in the International System of Units (SI) is:
questions.explain: From Ohm's law V = IR, resistance is measured in ohms.

questions.q: Ohm's law states the relation:
questions.explain: Ohm's law links voltage, current and resistance in a conductor at constant temperature.

questions.q: The speed of light in vacuum is:
questions.explain: Light travels at 3 lakh km per second; 343 m/s is the speed of sound in air — the usual distractor.

questions.q: The speed of sound in air at ordinary temperature is about:
questions.explain: Sound is much slower than light — that is why we see lightning before hearing thunder.

questions.q: Optical fibres, used in communication and endoscopy, work on the principle of:
questions.explain: Light repeatedly reflects totally inside the fibre and travels without much loss; a mirage is also caused by total internal reflection.

questions.q: The blue colour of the clear sky is due to:
options: Scattering of sunlight by air molecules
questions.explain: Air molecules scatter blue light the most (Rayleigh scattering), so the sky looks blue.

questions.q: A rainbow is formed due to:
options: Dispersion of sunlight by water droplets
questions.explain: Raindrops split white sunlight into seven colours by dispersion (with refraction and reflection inside the drop).

questions.q: Myopia (short-sight) is corrected by using a:
questions.explain: In myopia the image forms before the retina; a concave lens diverges the rays to correct it.

questions.q: Hypermetropia (long-sight) is corrected by using a:
questions.explain: A convex lens converges light so the image falls exactly on the retina.

questions.q: The power of a lens is measured in:
questions.explain: Power = 1/focal length (in metres); an optician's prescription is written in dioptres.

questions.q: The image formed by a plane mirror is:
questions.explain: A plane mirror gives a same-size virtual image that is left-right reversed (lateral inversion).

questions.q: At higher altitudes water boils at a lower temperature because:
questions.explain: Lower pressure lets water boil below 100°C, so cooking takes longer in the hills — hence the pressure cooker.

questions.q: A pressure cooker cooks food faster because inside it:
options: Higher pressure raises the boiling point of water
questions.explain: Under pressure, water can reach about 120°C, cooking food faster.

questions.q: An electric fuse wire must have:
options: Low melting point and high resistance
questions.explain: Excess current melts the fuse wire first and breaks the circuit, protecting appliances; it is connected in series.

questions.q: Silver is the best conductor of electricity, but household wiring uses copper mainly because silver is:
questions.explain: Copper is the practical choice — a good conductor, ductile and much cheaper than silver.

questions.q: Rubber and plastic are used as covering on electric wires because they are:
questions.explain: Insulators do not allow current to pass and protect us from shocks.

questions.q: A battery converts:
questions.explain: Cells store chemicals that react to produce electric current.

questions.q: An electric generator (dynamo) converts:
questions.explain: A generator works on electromagnetic induction; an electric motor does the reverse conversion.

questions.q: An electric motor converts:
questions.explain: Motors in fans, pumps and trains turn electrical energy into motion.

questions.q: The pH of a neutral solution at 25°C is:
questions.explain: Below 7 is acidic and above 7 is basic (alkaline); pure water is exactly 7.

questions.q: The acid present in the human stomach that helps digestion is:
questions.explain: Stomach HCl kills germs and activates enzymes; excess acidity is treated with mild bases called antacids.

questions.q: Vinegar, used in cooking and pickles, contains:
questions.explain: Vinegar is a dilute solution of acetic acid; lemon has citric acid and curd has lactic acid.

questions.q: The sour taste of lemon and oranges is due to:
questions.explain: Citrus fruits contain citric acid; tamarind contains tartaric acid.

questions.q: The acid that sours milk into curd is:
questions.explain: Lactobacillus bacteria convert milk sugar into lactic acid, setting the curd.

questions.q: Baking soda, used in cooking and antacids, is chemically:
questions.explain: NaHCO₃ is baking soda; Na₂CO₃ is washing soda and NaOH is caustic soda — the classic formula trap set.

questions.q: The chemical formula of washing soda is:
questions.explain: Washing soda is hydrated sodium carbonate; CaOCl₂ is bleaching powder.

questions.q: Caustic soda, used in soap making, is chemically:
questions.explain: NaOH is a strong alkali called caustic soda; KOH is caustic potash.

questions.q: Bleaching powder, used to disinfect water, has the formula:
questions.explain: Bleaching powder (calcium oxychloride) releases chlorine, which kills germs.

questions.q: The most abundant metal in the Earth's crust is:
questions.explain: Oxygen is the most abundant element overall; among metals, aluminium comes first, then iron.

questions.q: The most abundant element in the Earth's crust is:
questions.explain: Oxygen (about 46%) and silicon (about 28%) together make up most of the crust.

questions.q: Rusting of iron is a chemical change in which iron reacts with:
options: Oxygen and moisture to form hydrated iron oxide
questions.explain: Rust is Fe₂O₃·xH₂O; painting, oiling and galvanisation prevent rusting.

questions.q: Bronze, the alloy used for statues and medals, is a mixture of:
questions.explain: Brass = copper + zinc; bronze = copper + tin — a standard alloy pair.

questions.q: Brass, used for utensils and musical instruments, is an alloy of:
questions.explain: Brass is copper-zinc; solder is lead-tin, and stainless steel is iron-chromium-nickel.

questions.q: The main component of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) (Compressed Natural Gas) is:
questions.explain: Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) is mostly methane; Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) is mainly butane and propane.

questions.q: Hard water, which does not lather easily with soap, contains salts of:
questions.explain: Calcium and magnesium bicarbonates/chlorides/sulphates make water hard.
